description: The small dark disc preceding every assistant turn, marking it as the thinking partner rather than the person.
name: AgentAvatar

description: The transcript of what the stand-in agent actually called. This is the evidence that the panel drives the real bound catalog rather than a simulation: every reply is the tool's own, returned through the path a browser agent's call takes.
name: AgentCallLog

description: One call and what it returned. Monospace on the name and prose on the result, because the reply is written for an agent to read and is worth reading. A failure takes the risk colour so a broken call cannot be mistaken for a quiet one.
name: AgentCallLogRow

description: The band a person meets when they submit an idea and nothing picks it up. Before it existed the only sign of that was 'No agent attached' in the header, which states a fact about the page rather than telling the person what to do about it. It leads with the instruction and follows with the explanation, in that order, because someone who just pressed return wants to know what to DO - the panel used to open with the explanation and reach the prompt third, which read as a footnote about agent availability rather than as the next step. A renderer and a composer only: every string comes from handoffCopy where tests pin it, and the band itself is HandoffInstruction, CopyablePrompt, SeedIdeaQuote and HandoffFootnote in that order. What it decides is whether to appear at all - it hides when an agent is listening, using the identical predicate NodeQuestionComposer uses so working counts as attached and the two surfaces cannot contradict each other, and it hides when the log already carries an agent-origin event, because a map an agent has already worked is not waiting for one.
name: AgentHandoff

description: The collapsed dev panel, pinned to the corner: present enough to find, quiet enough to ignore. It sits over the map rather than in the layout because it is not part of the product.
name: AgentPanelLauncher

description: A stand-in agent for development and captures — not a mock. WebMCP is top-level-secure-context only and captures render in an iframe, so no real agent can ever attach where this product most needs demonstrating. It drives window.__thinkingMapAgent, the same bound catalog a real agent calls, so its scripted sequence exercises the genuine tool paths. Rendered outside production only.
name: AgentSimulator

description: Whether an agent can reach this page, stated plainly. Unavailable is the ordinary case rather than an error — WebMCP is top-level-secure-context only, so a preview iframe, Safari, and any page opened without a browser agent all land there. It sits in the header because presence is a fact about the whole page.
name: AgentStatus

description: The three states of agent presence as one dot: lime for attached, pulsing lime mid-call, and the plain line colour when none is attached. Absence gets a neutral treatment rather than a warning one, because here it is normal.
name: AgentStatusDot

description: Call one bound tool by hand with a small JSON input. The tool list comes from the published driver rather than a hardcoded array, so what it offers is exactly what is bound — a tool that failed to register is missing here too, which is the point.
name: AgentToolRunner

description: A question's suggested answers, as chips. Clicking one FILLS the answer box rather than submitting it — the rule SuggestionChips established on the landing screen, and the reason these are a head start rather than a set of choices. Deliberately not SuggestionChips itself, which is bound to the landing page's fixed list and has no per-question input.
name: AnswerChips

description: Just enough of the WebMCP bridge to record an answer. Narrowed deliberately: the answers hook has no business with tools or connection status, and the narrow shape is what lets a test hand it a plain function instead of standing up a context.
name: AnswerWriter

untestabilityReason.justification: A TypeScript interface — the narrowed slice of the WebMCP bridge the answers hook needs. It declares a shape and emits no runtime code, so there is nothing to execute; the behaviour behind it is covered by useMapAnswers.test.ts, which supplies this shape directly.

description: Wordmark left, phase track right. Shared by the landing screen and the map workspace so the two never drift.
name: AppHeader

description: The affordance on a brief section nobody has accounted for. Its visible label and its accessible name deliberately differ: the label is the section mark, because a heading can run to a full sentence and the spelled-out version wrapped to three lines in a 276px rail, while the accessible name keeps the heading, where length costs nothing and a bare section number would tell a screen-reader user nothing about what they are asking after.
name: AskAboutSectionButton

description: The line that says what sending this question will actually do. Its own component because it is the part of the composer that has to be honest: an asked question reaches an agent already waiting and reaches nobody otherwise. The wording itself lives in askPresence, where tests pin it.
name: AskPresenceNote

description: Renders what the bridge knows - whether an agent is attached, why not when it is not, the tools the page exposes, the questions an agent is waiting on, and the pending count. Exists so the bridge has something to show: WebMcpBridge renders only a context provider, so an isolated capture of it alone would be a blank frame. Its two buttons drive the REAL ask_user path through the headless driver and the real answer path back, so the AwaitingAnswer scenario captures the state the code actually produces rather than one staged to look like it.
name: BridgeReadout

untestabilityReason.justification: Lives under app/isolated-components/ and exists only to give that isolation route something to render. It is a presentational read of the bridge context; the state it displays is produced by WebMcpBridge, covered by the webmcpbridge-noagent scenario.

description: The panel's one sentence, and the bar under it. It leads with what is UNTOUCHED rather than what is covered, because the covered sections already have their evidence sitting next to this. The character count gets its own line because a count of sections understates the finding on its own - four short sections and four long ones are not the same news for a client.
name: BriefCoverageHeadline

description: Citations pointing at sections the brief does not have. Surfaced rather than swallowed: a dangling reference means the map and the document disagree about what the document contains, and a silently dropped citation would let the accounted-for count overstate itself - the one failure the whole panel exists to prevent. Renders nothing at all when there are none, so a healthy map pays nothing in space.
name: BriefDanglingNote

description: The way a twenty-page spec gets into a map. Owns one question - what document, if any, is attached - and shows exactly one of three things depending on the answer: the readout of an attached brief, the paste box, or the drop target. Extraction goes over the wire because reading a PDF is a server's job, and nothing is persisted by it, so a brief the person discards leaves nothing behind.
name: BriefDrop

description: The opening lines of the brief, exactly as extracted. Verbatim on purpose, markdown marks and all: the claim being made is this is what we got out of your file, and prettifying it would undermine the one thing it is here to prove. A file that yielded nothing shows nothing, which is the signal.
name: BriefExcerpt

description: The brief intake with its dashed panel removed: a hidden file picker its parent opens plus the one error line an upload can produce, and the ACCEPT list keeping the picker and the extractor in step. Renders nothing at rest.
name: BriefFileInput

untestabilityReason.justification: A headless forwardRef wrapper around a hidden file input plus one conditional error line - it renders nothing at rest, so an isolated capture would be a blank frame. The picker it opens is driven by BriefMenu (covered by BriefMenu.render.test.tsx) and the upload path is exercised by the landing application scenarios.

description: The whole brief intake stated in 28px of width instead of 140px of height: a + button inside the input frame opening a two-item menu (Upload a file / Paste a brief), which becomes a chip naming the document once one is attached. Closes on outside click, Escape, and selection.
name: BriefMenu

description: The client's brief beside the map, marked with what has been accounted for. A client who hands over a twenty-page spec wants evidence you read all of it; the map is the evidence for the sections it cites, and this panel exists for the ones it does not - the difference between reading a brief and inferring it. Pure composition over a header, a headline, the section list and a dangling-reference note. Its one piece of behaviour is the untouched-section prompt, which rides the existing user.note channel so it wakes a waiting agent with no new mechanism.
name: BriefPanel

description: What document this is and how much of it the map accounts for. The source name is the client's own filename rather than anything derived - a person recognises the thing they sent, and a tidied-up title would break that recognition for no gain. Truncated rather than wrapped, so a long filename cannot push the headline down the panel.
name: BriefPanelHeader

description: The other way in: paste the words. Not a fallback for when upload fails but a first-class door, because a client who cannot get their document out of the system it lives in still has the text, and the text is all this product ever wanted from the file.
name: BriefPasteBox

description: What we are holding, before any map exists. Says where the document came from, how much of it there is, and - through BriefExcerpt - what actually came out of the file, so a client finds out their PDF was a scan here rather than three questions into a map built on nothing.
name: BriefReadout

description: One section of the brief and what the map has to say about it. The weighting is deliberately the inverse of the obvious one: untouched sections carry the ink and accounted-for ones recede, because the covered sections already have their evidence beside the panel and rendering the one finding a client is owed as the quietest thing on screen would bury it. Not lime and not red on purpose - lime marks the one thing that just changed, and red would read as a defect rather than a prompt.
name: BriefSectionRow

description: What extraction wanted the person to know, in the risk colour. The safety net of the whole intake: where someone who uploaded a photograph of a document finds out no words came out of it. A warning rather than an error because nothing failed - their file is simply not what they thought, and they can still paste.
name: BriefWarning

description: What to build first, and what building it would prove. A numbered list of next steps is indistinguishable from a plan to build the whole thing in order - the failure this product exists to prevent - so this region leads with the smallest increment that would settle something, and a slice that settles nothing is marked in place rather than quietly filtered out. Sits above the next-steps track: what you build comes before what you go and find out.
name: BuildSequence

description: A what-we-know or what-we-don't-know card on the summary screen, falling back to the keep-talking hint when its bucket is empty.
name: BulletCard

description: The facts a card knows about itself that its eyebrow can name: kind, origin, brief section, whether it has been asked about, and whether it has been answered.
name: CardEyebrowFacts

untestabilityReason.justification: A TypeScript interface naming the facts a card's eyebrow can report. It declares a shape and emits no runtime code; every field is exercised through cardEyebrow in cardEyebrow.test.ts.

description: The mark in a card's top-right corner, naming its colour family. One glyph per FAMILY rather than per kind: eighteen glyphs would be a legend to learn, and the eyebrow beneath already names the exact kind — so the icon is the same six categories said a second way, which costs the reader nothing new. Drawn as inline SVG in the manner of Wordmark rather than pulled from a package; the design references put emoji in this slot, and emoji render differently on every platform and would be the only mark in the product this codebase did not draw. The magnifier is carried across from the retired node pill rather than redrawn.
name: CardIcon

description: Scaffold-shipped layout for the isolation-route tree, providing the centred capture frame and the production guard.
name: CodeYamIsolateLayout

untestabilityReason.justification: Shipped by the codeyam scaffolder and untouched by this project. It exists to host component captures; asserting anything about it would be testing the tooling rather than Thinking Map.

description: The two direct ways to put something into the map: a note the agent reads on its next turn, or a node that lands on the map. Deliberately not a chat box — one line, no history under it, and what you send goes to the activity rail rather than into a thread.
name: ContributionBar

description: Which of the two contributions the bar is composing. Two tabs rather than two stacked inputs, because the difference between them is what happens afterwards — that is a choice, not two separate controls.
name: ContributionTabs

description: A block of text whose whole purpose is to end up somewhere else. Its own component because it is the only part of the handoff band with behavior, and the behavior has a failure mode worth being deliberate about: clipboard access can be refused, and a copy button that silently does nothing is worse than one that never claimed to work. The text stays on screen either way, so there is always the select-and-copy path underneath. A tone prop defaults to the original secondary appearance and promotes to a lime-filled primary for the handoff band, so promoting that one caller cannot restyle the others. Promoted to the primary action on the arrival screen, the label flip is the entire success signal, so it sits in an aria-live region rather than being a purely visual confirmation.
name: CopyablePrompt

description: The strongest directions on the summary screen, lettered A onward so they can be referred to by name in conversation.
name: DirectionsCard

description: A compact fold: a summary line you press to reveal what is under it. A native <details> rather than a hook and a boolean — keyboard-operable and announced correctly with nothing wired up, working before hydration, and open/closed is a reading posture no other component needs to know about. It exists because the map became the whole surface, leaving the contribution bar and the activity rail with no column to live in.
name: Disclosure

description: The summary screen's empty state, phrased as the next action rather than the absence of data.
name: EmptyHint

description: Free text a side actually wrote, inside an activity row. A question keeps its weight here for the reason it did in the conversation panel this replaces: the questions are the product, and one buried in an agent's note is the line the person is meant to act on.
name: ExchangeNote

description: What has happened to this map, oldest first, from both sides in one ordered column. It records what was done to the artifact rather than reconstructing a conversation it cannot see, and scrolls to the end so the newest is where the attention goes.
name: ExchangeRail

description: The activity rail before anything has happened. It describes the next action rather than the absence of data — and that matters more than usual here, because it is the only cue a person arriving without an agent has that the map is something two parties write to.
name: ExchangeRailEmpty

description: One thing that happened to the map. A record, not a turn in a conversation: one line, marked with the side that caused it, and it does not invite a reply. The agent gets its dark disc; the person a hollow counterpart of the same size, so the rail reads as one column rather than two feeds.
name: ExchangeRow

description: The honest paragraph about why nobody is attached, and the two ways to fix that for good - kept, and kept small. Its own component because of the decision it owns: these two travel together and they travel BELOW the action. The panel used to lead with the explanation, which answered a question someone who just pressed return had not asked yet; deleting it would have been the other mistake, since it is the only thing on the page that says a map cannot summon a thinking partner. So it is demoted rather than dropped, and grouping it here is what makes demoted a structural fact instead of two loose paragraphs that could drift back up the page one edit at a time.
name: HandoffFootnote

description: What to do about a map nobody has picked up, said before anything explains why nobody has. Its own component because of the decision it owns: the steps are an ORDERED list, not a styled pair of lines. Their order is the content - copy, then paste - and someone skimming a band on arrival reads the numbers before they read the words, so rendering them unordered or as prose would lose the only thing that makes two short sentences into instructions. It is also the block whose POSITION is the point: the panel used to open with the explanation and reach the prompt third, and keeping this separable is what lets a test assert that ordering rather than merely assert both texts exist somewhere.
name: HandoffInstruction

description: The landing route. Reads every saved map and composes the header with the landing screen - imports and composition only, no markup of its own.
name: Home

description: The single free-text input the whole product starts from, with its large send button. No structured fields - the point is that you can arrive with something vague.
name: IdeaForm

description: The oversized question the landing screen opens with, plus its one-line invitation. One of the two showcase moments in the design system.
name: IdeaHero

description: The entry point. Owns the submit state for the free-text idea input and the starter chips, and routes to the new map on success.
name: IdeaPrompt

description: Somewhere to put the next thought, under the finished plan. The summary is the end of the loop and deliberately not a dead end. There are no open questions on this screen by definition, so it is the contribution bar and the record without the waiting-on-you panel.
name: KeepThinkingPanel

description: The whole landing surface: the question, the idea input, and anything already saved.
name: LandingScreen

description: The one channel on mapEvents that is not a map id. Every other emit is keyed by mapId, which cannot carry news of a map no waiter knows the id of yet - and that is exactly what a newly started map is. A constant rather than a literal because a waiter subscribed to a typo'd string would simply never wake, which is indistinguishable from nobody having submitted anything.
name: MAP_CREATED

untestabilityReason.justification: A single string constant naming an event channel; the behaviour that depends on it is covered by the waitForNewMap tests in app/lib/exchange.integration.test.ts.

description: What useMapAnswers returns: every question's current answer, and the function that records one. The recorder is optional because an isolated scenario has no exchange to write to — the map still reads correctly there, it simply cannot be answered.
name: MapAnswers

untestabilityReason.justification: A TypeScript interface describing what useMapAnswers returns. It declares a shape and emits no runtime code; the values it describes are asserted in useMapAnswers.test.ts.

description: One node on the map, as a card. The card replaced the pill because a pill could only ever hold a label, and the thing a question most needs to hold is the answer to it — so the body is one of three things: what a statement node says, the affordance for an unanswered question, or the answer to one somebody has answered. Fill is deliberately neutral on every card; which card wears the lime belongs to the card-visual plan.
name: MapCard

description: The answering affordance inside a question card — the change the whole plan is for, since the question and the place you answer it are now one object rather than a dashed pill on a map and a row in a panel beside it. Holds its own draft because each card owns exactly one answer, and swaps to the recorded answer once there is one.
name: MapCardAnswer

description: The line above a card's title, naming what the card is. Presentational only: which words go in the line is cardEyebrow's business, because that is string logic with a rule worth testing rather than anything about rendering.
name: MapCardEyebrow

description: The top line of a card: which round it arrived in, and which family it is. The two marks sit at opposite corners and take the same colour on purpose — a card can be clipped by the edge of the column or by a narrow viewport, so putting the family colour at both ends means whichever corner survives still says what kind of thing this is. The root is the exception: its marker stays neutral grey, because the subject family's colour is ink and ink on a round number would read as emphasis on the number rather than as a category.
name: MapCardHeader

description: The map on day one. Per the design system an empty state describes what happens next rather than reporting an absence, so it says the map fills in as you answer. Deliberately not EmptyHint, which renders an <li> for the summary screen's list and would be invalid markup inside the map's column.
name: MapEmptyState

description: The map route. Loads one thinking map with its whole exchange log, and switches between the working map and the summary screen on the phase, deriving the live-map caption from the current nodes. The log is read here rather than fetched later because the map is drawn from it: which nodes arrived together is what makes a round, and a round is what makes a row.
name: MapPage

description: One round of thinking, as a row: everything in it arrived together, and the next round appears below it — the whole of what 'the map builds downward' means. The band wraps rather than scrolling sideways, which is what makes one layout work at every width with no breakpoint deciding which it is in.
name: MapRow

description: The whole map surface: the header with agent presence, and whichever view the phase calls for. The working tree while the thinking is live, the plan once it has run out — the same map at two moments, which is why choosing between them lives here rather than in the route.
name: MapScreen

description: The working view - conversation left, map right - the two views of the same thinking placed side by side.
name: MapWorkspace

description: The concrete next steps, arrowed left to right. The first step is unboxed because it is where you start tomorrow rather than one option among several.
name: NextStepsTrack

description: Which kind of node the person is adding. It reads the same controlled vocabulary the agent's tools are bound to, so a node a person adds is indistinguishable in kind from one the agent added — which is what makes the map genuinely co-authored. Its labels are the map's own eyebrows.
name: NodeKindPicker

description: Asking the agent about one specific node. Carries the node id, so the question arrives already attached to the thing it is about rather than leaving the agent to work out from prose which pill was meant. The send control and the note beneath it state whether an agent is actually listening, because WebMCP is pull-only and implying a reply is coming when nothing is attached is the one thing this feature could genuinely mislead about.
name: NodeQuestionComposer

description: What the composer is about, and the way out of it. The node's own words are repeated from the pill because the composer covers part of the map, and someone mid-sentence should not have to move it to remember which node they clicked. The label truncates rather than wrapping, since nothing constrains how long an agent writes one.
name: NodeQuestionHeader

description: One node's arrangement as a client would ask for it. Vestigial: the map is a scrolling column of card rows with no plane to drag a node around on, so nothing produces one any more.
name: Nudge

untestabilityReason.justification: A TypeScript interface describing one node's arrangement as a client would request it. It declares a shape and emits no runtime code; parseNudges, which produces it, is covered by route.test.ts.

description: The placeholder band. Its geometry mirrors MapRow's exactly — same wrap, gap, and card min/max/height — so the placeholders stand where the real cards will and the row does not jump sideways when they arrive; that coupling is the point, which is why the numbers are repeated rather than approximated. The cards are aria-hidden, but the shimmer IS a message, so it is also said in words to a live region for a reader who cannot see it.
name: PendingCards

description: What the wait turned out to mean, in one line. Its own component for the same reason AskPresenceNote is: this is the part of the pending row that has to be honest, and a sentence that has to be honest is worth being able to point at. The wording lives in pendingRow, where tests pin it.
name: PendingNote

description: The row the map reaches for before it has one — the whole of what 'the app moves first' means. A round gets finished and the next row appears immediately as placeholders, so the column visibly grows downward instead of sitting still. It must never imply an agent is writing, because the page cannot start anyone's turn, so the shimmer is bounded and resolves into whichever of three sentences is actually true.
name: PendingRow

description: The one action worth taking when a phase's work is done, at the bottom of the round you just finished rather than up in the chrome — with the map drawn as a column you answer in place, the eye is already there. Sentence and label both come from PHASE_ASK beside the phase labels, so the step the nav names and the step this offers to leave cannot drift apart; what the press does lives in useAdvancePhase.
name: PhaseAdvance

description: The phase track. The active phase wears the lime; completed phases are deliberately not distinguished from upcoming ones, because this is a map of the process and not a progress bar. Below lg the track scrolls horizontally rather than collapsing to a summary, and its edge fades are derived from scroll position - each one appears only when there is genuinely more track past that edge, so the fade never washes out the active pill on a track that fits.
name: PhaseNav

description: What the person said, shown back in the card's body. The Edit affordance is deliberately quiet — the eyebrow's weight rather than a button's — because an answered question is settled and reopening it should be available without being an invitation.
name: RecordedAnswer

description: The document shell: html and body, the global stylesheet, and the page metadata. Scaffold-shipped; this project changed only the title and description.
name: RootLayout

untestabilityReason.justification: Framework-required document shell generated by the stack template. It renders its children inside html/body and carries the metadata export - there is no behaviour of this project's own to assert, and every application scenario renders through it.

description: One round of thinking as the map draws it: a 1-based index shown to the person as the card's marker, the nodes that arrived together, and the phase this round opened when it opened one.
name: Round

untestabilityReason.justification: A TypeScript interface describing one round as the map draws it. It declares a shape and emits no runtime code; its values are asserted throughout mapRounds.test.ts.

description: What to do when the round is done, under the round it is done with. Composition and one choice: the count while there is still answering to do, the phase's action once nothing more is coming, and deliberately NOTHING in between — while the map is still reaching, the shimmering row above is already saying it, and a second line one line apart was the first thing that looked wrong on screen. No presence line lives here for the same reason.
name: RowFooter

description: How far through the round you are, as a count with no action beside it. A button here would invite skipping past questions the person has not looked at — while a round is still being answered, the cards ARE the action.
name: RowProgress

description: The curves between the card rows: one short thread per card, rising from the card above that prompted it, in the child's family colour. Drawn as ONE overlay across the whole column rather than a layer per row gap — the rows are a CSS flex wrap, so there are no computed coordinates anywhere and every thread has to be measured off the DOM either way; a single overlay does that in one coordinate space with one ResizeObserver. It holds the measurement and the rendering only, with the shape of a thread living in threadGeometry. Purely decorative and aria-hidden, since a thread restates what the rows and eyebrows already carry in text.
name: RowThreads

description: A contiguous run of node-adds from one side of the exchange, with the revision span it covers so a phase set can be attributed to the round that closed it.
name: Run

untestabilityReason.justification: A TypeScript interface, internal to the round grouping, describing a contiguous run of node-adds and the revision span it covers. It declares a shape and emits no runtime code; the grouping it serves is covered by mapRounds.test.ts.

description: The Pick up where you left off list. Renders nothing at all when there are no saved maps, so day one stays clean.
name: SavedMapList

description: One saved thinking map on the landing screen, showing the phase it reached and how many nodes it holds.
name: SavedMapRow

description: Scaffold-shipped route that resolves a scenario slug to its url and redirects, so a scenario can be opened by name in development.
name: ScenarioRedirectPage

untestabilityReason.justification: Shipped by the codeyam scaffolder and untouched by this project. It is development-only tooling - it calls notFound in production - and belongs to the editor's surface rather than the product's.

description: The person's own words, handed back to them. Its own component because of the decision it owns: a map started from a document rather than a sentence has no seed idea, and rendering empty quote marks around nothing would look like the text was lost - the precise anxiety this panel exists to answer. Blank in, nothing out.
name: SeedIdeaQuote

description: The lime circular send control with its arrow, positioned inside whichever input pill hosts it. Shared by the landing prompt and the conversation reply box.
name: SendButton

description: One increment in the build sequence: what you build, what it would prove, and roughly what it costs. Its own component so each state - validated, proves nothing, dangling link - gets an isolated scenario, following the BulletCard / DirectionsCard split. The effort note is the agent's own sentence printed as written: nothing parses or validates it, because a rough claim a human can argue with is more honest than a number that merely looks computed.
name: SliceCard

description: The four starter chips. Clicking one fills the prompt rather than submitting it, so the person finishes the sentence in their own words.
name: SuggestionChips

description: The summary screen's opening declaration that the product was not built - the honesty the whole tool is organised around.
name: SummaryHeadline

description: The end of the loop, and deliberately not a dead end: the summary with the conversation still open beneath it so the map can keep moving.
name: SummaryScreen

description: The final screen composed whole: the declaration, the three cards, the build sequence and the next-steps track - what you build first coming before what you go and find out. Composition only; the sorting lives in groupSummaryNodes and the slice resolution in buildSequence.
name: SummaryView

description: The map: a single column of rows growing downward, scrolled like a page — and reaching for the next row before anyone asks it to. It was once a tidy tree on a zoomable plane; the tree is still in the data (parentId and order are untouched, the tool contract unchanged) but a column that grows downward is navigated by scrolling, so the zoom, pan, fit and fold all went. Composition only: rounds come from mapRounds, progress from roundProgress, what may honestly be claimed while waiting from pendingRow, the clock bounding that wait from useBoundedWait, and following the column down from useFollowColumn.
name: ThinkingMapView

description: A stand-in for the map column, so RowThreads can be looked at on its own. The overlay measures the DOM — it asks where the cards ended up after a flex wrap and draws between them — so it renders nothing without laid-out cards to measure, and mounting it bare would capture an empty frame. This gives it the two things it needs and nothing else: an element to hold the ref, and labelled boxes carrying data-node-id in a wrapping band. Plain rectangles rather than real MapCards, because what the scenarios are for is the threads, and full cards would put 240px of text in front of them.
name: ThreadsHarness

untestabilityReason.justification: Capture harness under app/isolated-components/, existing only so RowThreads has cards to measure in isolation. Not reachable from the app.

description: Mounts the page's own front door. Binds the tool catalog to the current map for as long as the map page is open, disposing on unmount and on map change because re-registering a live tool name throws InvalidStateError. Holds the pending ask_user state and resolves the agent's turn when the person answers, writing the answer to the log BEFORE releasing it so an agent that already gave up still finds it. Publishes the headless driver whether or not a real agent is present, which is the only way the tools are reachable inside a capture iframe. Reports connection state through the same context, and exposes the tool names from the catalog rather than from the published driver - a consumer's effect runs before its parent's, so reading the driver would race the binding that creates it.
name: WebMcpBridge

description: The product mark: three nodes and the connectors between them, doubling as the link home from every screen.
name: Wordmark

description: Puts the person's node on the map, with origin 'user' — the same fact the pill reads to badge it and the tools read to avoid re-ingesting their own writes. With no parent named it hangs off the root, because a second root would read as a second idea; an unknown kind falls back to one the map can draw, and an empty label writes nothing.
name: addUserNode

description: The node ids a user.answer event closed. Same payload tolerance as questionIds, and the input to both the suppression rule and the answered-question count.
name: answeredIds

description: What the agent is told once the person has answered. Reports each question alongside its answer, because an agent that asked several cannot match them up from the answers alone.
name: answeredResponse

description: The latest answer per question id, read off the exchange log rather than the node — the node's status records that a question is settled, the log holds what was actually said. Latest wins because editing an answer IS posting another one, which is what makes an edit take effect and edit history free. A malformed entry is skipped rather than blanking every other answer.
name: answersByNodeId

description: Reads the id/answer pairs out of a user.answer payload sent by the browser. Untrusted on this side of the wire, so a malformed payload yields an empty list rather than throwing.
name: answersOf

description: Thin executor for a validated map-mutation plan: walks the inserts in order, resolving each temporary ref to the real id the database just returned so one call can create a parent and its children together, then applies updates and any phase change. A slice's testsRef goes through the same resolution as parentRef, since a slice usually names an assumption created moments earlier in the same call; an unresolvable value is written through rather than dropped, because a dangling link is reported on screen and losing it silently would hide that the slice claimed to settle anything. All the rules live in planMapMutations, which is pure and tested. It has a second output - every write also becomes an ordered event on the map's log, tagged with the origin that made it - which is what lets a person and an agent work the same map without either being told what the other did. Only changes that actually landed are logged, since an event for a node that was not there would be a revision no agent could reconcile.
name: applyToolCalls

description: Turns a character count into an approximate page count at roughly 1,800 characters per page, so a person is shown a unit they think in. Anything with text in it is at least one page; an empty document is zero.
name: approxPages

description: The copy that says what sending a node question will actually do. WebMCP is pull-only, so asking wakes an agent already parked on await_user_activity and reaches nobody otherwise; this returns the send label and the note for each case, so the one thing the feature could mislead about is pinned by tests rather than read off a screenshot.
name: askPresence

description: The nodes the person has asked about, derived from the log rather than tracked beside it, so the marks survive a reload and count questions asked from any front door. A malformed or missing nodeId is skipped rather than throwing.
name: askedNodeIds

description: Offers the exchange log as a subscribable MCP resource. Deliberately speculative: resource subscriptions are an open proposal, so this no-ops on every browser that exists today. Same feature-detection shape as bindTools, and kept in the only file allowed to name navigator.modelContext.
name: bindExchangeResource

untestabilityReason.justification: branches entirely on navigator.modelContext.registerResource, an unshipped W3C proposal no browser or polyfill implements; every reachable path today is the no-op, so a test could only assert against a hand-built fake of an API whose shape is not yet settled

description: Registers the catalog with the browser agent for one map and returns a disposer. The WebMCP draft has already moved once - provideContext was removed in the March 2026 revision in favour of registerTool/unregisterTool, while the polyfill still ships the older shape - so both conventions are handled here, the one file that names navigator.modelContext. Re-registering a live name throws InvalidStateError, which is why unregister-then-register is the only safe update path and why the disposer exists.
name: bindTools

description: Builds the HTTP and stdio front doors from the shared tool catalog rather than a hand-written list, which is what stops the three doors drifting apart. Loops the catalog, splicing a mapId argument onto each tool's own schema and stripping it back off before handing the call to the shared runtime - out here the agent has no page, so it must name the map it means. Adds the two whole-collection tools that belong only to the server doors, list_thinking_maps and create_thinking_map, since a page is already scoped to one map. Built fresh per request in the stateless HTTP mode.
name: buildMcpServer

untestabilityReason.justification: Registration only: it constructs an SDK server object and attaches handlers that delegate to runTool, whose behaviour is covered by its own entry and the mid-exchange scenario, and to createMap/listMaps which have theirs. The catalog it loops over is covered by app/lib/toolCatalog.test.ts. The wiring was verified end to end over both transports.

description: Resolves a finished map's slices into the order they should be built in, each entry carrying the node it would settle. The whole opinion of the build sequence lives in its provesNothing flag: an increment that tests no assumption is not a validating slice but work scheduled early, so it is marked rather than filtered out, and a slice whose target has since been deleted is reported as dangling rather than rendered as a blank. Pure - nodes in, an ordered list out - so every interesting case is a test rather than a screenshot.
name: buildSequence

description: The descriptors handed to a browser agent, one per catalog tool. Separated from registration so that WHAT the agent is offered can be checked without a navigator.modelContext: registering is a boundary call, but the set being registered is a contract. Each descriptor is bound to its own tool name, and annotations are carried only where the catalog declares them.
name: buildToolDescriptors

description: Runs one tool on behalf of an agent attached to the page: validate, forward to the tools route because the implementations reach SQLite, and for ask_user perform the middle step only a page can do - putting the question to a person and recording their answer. Every decision it makes is delegated to toolInvocation; what remains here is the fetch and the wait.
name: callCatalogTool

description: The line a card uses to say what it is: the node's kind, then who wrote it, then whether it has been asked about, then the brief section it came from, in that fixed order. The rule with teeth is that an answered question stops calling itself Open — leaving the kind's default would have the card label the answer printed directly beneath it as unanswered.
name: cardEyebrow

description: Which card prompted which — one thread per card, from the card in the round directly above it, and nothing otherwise. Deliberately narrower than the parent-child graph the retired tree drew: the layout is rows now, so the rows already carry the structure and a full edge graph would be a thicket crossing the column. A card whose parent is more than one round back, or has no parent, or whose parent is not on the map, draws nothing — the honest picture for 'nothing prompted this here' is no line.
name: cardThreads

description: Counts which sections of a client's brief the map actually accounts for. Pure by design - sections and nodes in, counts out, no database and no brief text on the way out - because the whole point is that coverage is COUNTED from the nodes that cite each section, never asserted by an agent. Reports the untouched sections and how much document they represent, since a section count alone understates the finding, and surfaces citations pointing at sections the brief does not have rather than dropping them, which would let the accounted-for count quietly overstate itself. A heading with nothing under it counts toward neither half.
name: computeBriefCoverage

description: Turns one contribution from the page into the events that should be recorded for it, performing the map writes it implies. A note is only ever an event; an answer also closes its question, and a node is created first so the event can carry its real id.
name: contributionEvents

description: Starts a map from an unstructured idea, keeping the text verbatim as both the root node and the person's first message so the conversation and the map are two views of the same thing from the first turn. Truncates only the display title. The seed idea is the person's, so the root node and opening message are user-origin - an agent reading the log must not mistake the human's starting idea for something it wrote. Records the root as the map's first event, leaving it at revision 1: a new map at revision 0 with an empty log would give an agent no way to tell it from one it had already read to the end.
name: createMap

description: The map's current revision for a caller that needs only the cursor and not the events - used by the waiting tools to report where to resume from, and by the conflict check before it decides whether reading the log is warranted at all.
name: currentRevision

description: The cubic path from a parent card's bottom edge to a child card's top edge. Both control points are pulled vertically off their endpoints and never horizontally, so the thread leaves the card it came from going down and arrives at the next one going down — that is what produces the S-travel of the design references instead of a rope slung between two points, and what keeps a thread readable when the two cards are far apart across a wide row.
name: curve

description: Turns a stored row into a readable event. SQLite has no JSON column, so payloads are strings that could be anything; a payload that will not parse degrades to null rather than throwing, because one bad row must not take down the whole catch-up read an agent depends on. The revision and kind survive regardless.
name: decodeEvent

description: How deep a node sits in the tree, following parentId upward. Used only by the round grouping's fallback, for a map whose history was never recorded. Stops rather than hanging on a cycle or a missing parent, so a half-written map still groups.
name: depthOf

description: Names a new map from whatever the person gave us. With a brief, prefers its first markdown heading, then its first non-empty line - so the root pill reads as a title instead of a 57-character slice of a twenty-page spec. Without a brief it is the original behaviour unchanged: the seed idea, clipped to 60 characters.
name: deriveTitle

description: The rail line for one event that does not collapse — a note, an answer, a question, a phase change. The wording is the interface: it is the only account a person gets of what an agent did to their map, so it lives in one place and is pinned by tests.
name: describeEvent

description: The rail line for a collapsed run of node adds or updates. A run of one keeps the node's label, because naming the thing beats counting it; past one the count is the information.
name: describeRun

description: Marks a response as a genuine fault. Deliberately narrow: a conflict or a timeout is a normal result the agent is expected to reason about, and flagging those as errors would invite the blind retry the conflict path exists to prevent.
name: errorResponse

description: The exchange log's MCP resource URI, one per map, so a subscriber is subscribed to a specific map rather than to 'the exchange' in the abstract. Kept in the file that owns every navigator.modelContext name, so the registration and the notification cannot drift to different URIs.
name: exchangeUri

untestabilityReason.justification: a single template string with no branching or input handling; the URI shape is exercised through its only two callers, bindExchangeResource and notifyExchangeUpdated, whose own behaviour is platform-glue against an unshipped browser API

description: The lower-cased extension of a filename, or empty when it has none. Needed because browsers are inconsistent about the media type they attach to a .md - several send application/octet-stream - so the extension is the fallback the type dispatch falls back to.
name: extensionOf

untestabilityReason.justification: Private to a module that imports server-only plus unpdf and mammoth, so the file cannot load under vitest to reach it. Exercised end to end instead: real .pdf, .docx, .md and .txt uploads were extracted through the running app, including a .md sent as application/octet-stream, which is the case this helper exists for.

description: Gets the words out of whatever the client sent - PDF via unpdf, .docx via mammoth, markdown and plain text decoded directly - dispatching on media type and falling back to the file extension, because browsers are inconsistent about the type they attach to a .md. Server-only, and the single place any format-specific dependency is reached. Reads the buffer's size before extracting, since pdfjs detaches it.
name: extractBriefText

untestabilityReason.justification: The module imports server-only plus unpdf and mammoth, so it does not load under vitest at all. Its decision logic is extracted into the pure, tested extractionWarning and normalizeBriefText; what remains is dispatch and two library calls. The format paths were verified end to end against the running app with real .pdf, .docx, .md and .txt uploads, including a scanned-PDF case.

description: Pulls the raw text out of a .docx through mammoth, discarding the formatting. A brief is words; the Word file it arrived in is packaging.
name: extractDocx

untestabilityReason.justification: A wrapper around mammoth inside a server-only module that does not load under vitest. Verified against the running app with a real .docx upload, which extracted its four paragraphs intact.

description: Pulls the text out of a PDF through unpdf, merging pages into one string. unpdf rather than pdf-parse because pdf-parse runs a debug branch at import that reads a fixture off disk and fails in a bundled server runtime. Note that pdfjs transfers the buffer to its worker and detaches it, so the caller must read the size first.
name: extractPdf

untestabilityReason.justification: A wrapper around unpdf inside a server-only module that does not load under vitest. Verified against the running app with two real PDFs: a healthy 924-byte document extracted 299 characters, and an 80KB document stripped of its text extracted 10 and correctly raised the scanned-PDF warning.

description: Decides whether an extraction failed and says so in a sentence the person can act on: nothing at all came out, or a large file yielded almost no text - the scanned-PDF signature. Pure and separate from the extractor so the safety net of the whole intake is testable, and because the size it takes must be measured before extraction: pdfjs transfers the upload buffer to its worker and detaches it.
name: extractionWarning

description: The colour a card's family draws its icon and its thread in, as a CSS variable reference rather than a class name — for the SVG thread layer and the icon, which need a paint value. Pro and risk resolve to their own two colours rather than a shared judgment hue, for the same reason nodeShellClasses keeps them apart: a thread rising to a risk should be the risk colour, not a family average.
name: familyLineVar

description: A node kind's colour family, via KIND_FAMILY. The eighteen kinds collapse into six families because one hue per kind would be a legend rather than a system, and the eyebrow above every card already names the exact kind for anyone who wants the precision. KIND_FAMILY is a total Record on purpose, so a nineteenth kind will not compile until it is given a family; this wrapper adds the runtime half of that safety, since kinds also arrive from the database and from the model unvalidated — an unrecognised one falls back to the neutral ground family rather than losing its colour entirely.
name: familyOf

description: Where along a parent card's bottom edge each of its threads departs. Every thread starting at the same point is what turns four curves into one frayed rope — they overlap for the first stretch and only separate once already travelling sideways — so the departures are fanned evenly across the card's own bottom edge, symmetric about its centre and inset from the rounded corners. The caller passes its threads in the order of the children they land on, which is what keeps one parent's threads from crossing each other.
name: fanOrigins

description: Read one non-empty string field off an event payload, or null. The single guard every rail reader goes through, so an unparseable row degrades to a plainer line rather than throwing.
name: field

description: The user-origin changes to one node that landed after the revision an agent last read. Empty means the write is safe; non-empty means the person touched this node and the caller must decline instead of overwriting. Narrowed twice on purpose: an agent's own earlier writes are not a conflict with itself, and a busy map moves constantly so only a change to THIS node can clobber THIS write.
name: findConflictingChanges

description: Resolves a tool by name from the shared catalog. Every front door goes through it, and an unknown name comes back undefined so the caller can answer the agent rather than throw.
name: findTool

description: The text of the first answer in a user.answer payload. Only shown when a single question was answered — with several, a row has no way to say which answer belongs to which question.
name: firstAnswer

description: The first n non-empty lines of a document, for the intake's proof-of-extraction preview. Blank lines are skipped rather than counted, so a brief that opens with a heading and two blank lines still previews as three real lines.
name: firstLines

description: A character count with grouped thousands. A bare 12690 reads as an identifier sitting in a column of otherwise short numbers; grouped, it reads as an amount, which is the only reason it is shown.
name: formatCharCount

description: Renders one map in full for an MCP client - the verbatim seed idea, the conversation, and the indented node tree - so a client sees both views of the thinking the way the UI shows them side by side.
name: formatMapDetail

description: Renders the map list for an MCP client, leading every row with the id because that is what the client passes back to every other tool, and saying so plainly when there are no maps yet.
name: formatMapList

description: Renders what await_new_map handed back, for an agent that arrives with no context about the map at all. Every row leads with the id and spells out the next call rather than leaving it to be inferred: read_brief when the map was started from a document, read_map otherwise. An expiry gets its own branch - no new maps yet plus the cursor to resume from - so an agent looping on this never reads the ordinary case as a failure.
name: formatNewMaps

description: Sends a page-side tool call to the tools route, where the shared runtime executes it. The page cannot run the catalog itself because every implementation ends in SQLite, so this one hop is the only difference between the page door and the two server doors.
name: forward

untestabilityReason.justification: A single fetch plus a non-2xx guard that turns a transport failure into a readable message. What it sends is decided by validateToolInput and what it receives is produced by runTool, both covered by their own entries.

description: Loads a map's brief including its text - the one reader allowed to want it. Everything else takes the metadata that getMap selects, so tens of thousands of characters never reach a page render or a full read_map.
name: getBrief

untestabilityReason.justification: A one-line Prisma findUnique with no branching. The behaviour actually worth pinning is that getMap excludes the brief text while read_map still announces it, which mcpFormat.test.ts covers.

description: Loads a map's brief and returns its coverage by the nodes on that map, ready to render. The thin database half of computeBriefCoverage, kept here so that module stays pure and testable. Returns only headings and counts - never the brief's text - so rendering the panel on the server does not put a document of tens of thousands of characters on the wire. Null when the map has no brief, which the workspace renders by mounting no panel at all.
name: getBriefCoverage

description: Reads one map with its full conversation and node tree in creation order. The single read behind the workspace, the summary screen and the MCP get_thinking_map tool.
name: getMap

description: Groups a map's nodes into the rounds that produced them — one round per write, read off the exchange log, because nodes written together share a contiguous run of revisions and one origin. Deliberately NOT grouped by tree depth: an agent's second batch of questions usually lands at the same depth as its first, so by depth the two turns would collapse into one row. The root idea is always its own first round, and nodes the log never mentions fall back to depth grouping so a seeded or pre-existing map still draws.
name: groupIntoRounds

description: Sorts a finished map's nodes into the regions of the summary screen - known, unknown, directions, next steps and the build sequence's slices - ignoring every other kind and ordering each bucket by its stored order, because the steps and the slices are both numbered on screen. Slices sit beside the next steps rather than replacing them: a next step can be to interview three teachers, which is not something you build.
name: groupSummaryNodes

description: The MCP HTTP endpoint. Builds a fresh server and transport per request so concurrent clients never share transport state, then hands the request to the transport.
name: handle

untestabilityReason.justification: Four straight-line statements with no branching: construct server, construct transport, connect, delegate. The tools underneath are covered by their own entries, and the endpoint was verified end to end against a live MCP client - initialize, tools/list, and a create/add-node/read round trip.

description: What a map with nobody working on it says for itself, in words. WebMCP is pull-only, so submitting an idea writes a map but does not summon anyone to think about it, and the tempting thing to show - a spinner, 'getting started' - would be a lie about work that will never begin on its own. The wording lives here rather than as strings inside a component because the wording IS the interface and a regression here is a person being told something is happening when nothing is. It carries the instruction the panel leads with and the two steps it breaks down into - copy the prompt, paste it into your agent's chat window - alongside the eyebrow, the honest explanation, the attach hint, and the start prompt itself. hasBrief is an argument rather than a branch in the component because a brief-only map has no sentence to quote and pointing that agent at read_map would send it to the emptier of the two things it could read.
name: handoffCopy

description: Stands in for a heading when a passage has none: the first nine words of its opening line, elided if there were more. A person scanning the outline needs to recognise the passage, not read it.
name: impliedHeading

description: Guard for the eight kinds the exchange log can record. A kind outside the set would become a row that nothing knows how to render or resume past.
name: isEventKind

description: Type guard for the node kinds the map knows how to draw. Used to drop a hallucinated kind at the planning stage rather than storing a node no component has a treatment for.
name: isNodeKind

description: Type guard for the three node statuses. Status drives the visual treatment, so an unrecognised value is normalised rather than allowed to fall through to the default silently.
name: isNodeStatus

description: Type guard for the five phases of the loop. SQLite has no enums, so phase strings arrive from the database and from model tool calls unvalidated; this is what keeps an unknown value out of the phase nav. It deliberately answers a NARROWER question than normalizePhase: whether a value is literally one of the five current phases, which is what the tool schema validates against. A stored phase from before deconstruct and map merged is not one of them, and goes through normalizePhase instead.
name: isPhase

description: Whether a round is mostly research, finding or gap — the rule that decides which row gets its own banded territory rather than just its own card colour. Strictly more than half, so an even split does not band: a round with no majority has nothing to name it after. 'Mostly' rather than 'all' because a research round that picked up one stray question is still a research round, and demanding purity would mean the band never appeared on a real map. The root round never bands, since enclosing the map's subject as 'what already exists' would misdescribe it.
name: isResearchRound

description: Guard for the three kinds a browser is allowed to write. This is a trust boundary rather than a convenience: the page posts these directly, so accepting an agent-side kind here would let a page forge the other half of the conversation.
name: isUserEventKind

description: Whether a browser agent can actually reach this page: a model context exists, the context is secure, and the page is top level. All three are real gates - WebMCP is top-level-secure-context only, so the codeyam capture iframe fails the last one by design in every preview and scenario.
name: isWebMcpAvailable

description: Lists every thinking map newest-first with its phase and node/message counts. Backs the landing screen's Pick up where you left off list and the MCP list_thinking_maps tool.
name: listMaps

description: The stdio entrypoint for MCP clients that launch the server as a child process, such as Claude Desktop. Serves the same buildMcpServer over a stdio transport; only the transport differs from the HTTP route.
name: main

untestabilityReason.justification: A process entrypoint: build the server, connect a stdio transport, log readiness to stderr because stdout is the JSON-RPC channel. No branching. Verified by driving a real initialize and tools/list handshake through the process over a pipe.

description: The production seed entrypoint, deliberately a no-op. CodeYam projects start with an empty production database and let each scenario carry its own seed, so there is nothing to plant here.
name: main

untestabilityReason.justification: Scaffold-shipped entrypoint left as the no-op the CodeYam data model calls for: production starts empty and scenarios carry their own seeds. There is no behaviour to assert because the function deliberately does nothing.

description: Derives the line beside LIVE MAP from the current nodes so the map narrates itself truthfully: a bare seed, a count of open questions, an answered/open split, or the reassurance that nothing was lost after a direction change. Excludes the root idea from the answered count, and lets a just-updated node outrank the arithmetic.
name: mapCaption

description: Whether the map named in the URL is real, checked before either verb touches the log. Both GET and POST answer 404 rather than minting a revision against a map that does not exist.
name: mapExists

untestabilityReason.justification: A bare findUnique selecting only the id, coerced to a boolean. The work is the database call itself; the route behaviour it guards is covered by the exchange route's own probes and the mid-exchange scenario.

description: Reads navigator.modelContext, or null where there is none. The single place the WebMCP global is touched, so the draft spec moving again is one edit rather than a sweep.
name: modelContext

untestabilityReason.justification: A guarded read of a browser global that exists only in Chrome 146+. The availability decisions built on it - isWebMcpAvailable and webMcpUnavailableReason - are covered by app/lib/webmcp.test.ts, which stubs this same global.

description: Whether a guarded write warrants reading the log at all. An unguarded write is the agent saying it does not care, and a map that has not moved cannot have a conflict, so neither case costs a read.
name: needsConflictCheck

description: The node a question is about, if it is genuinely on this map. The same ownership check mapExists makes, pushed down to the payload so a caller cannot ask about a node belonging to someone else's map; returns the label too, because the rail names the node.
name: nodeOnMap

description: Picks the shell classes for a map card, encoding the design system rule that must not break: status beats kind. The precedence is root, then updated, then open, then kind colour, then answered — so an unanswered question is dashed and unfilled whatever family it belongs to, and exactly one card wears the lime. Kind colour slots in at the accent tier and nowhere above it: pro and risk keep their own two colours because the pair points opposite ways, and every other kind takes its family line and near-white tint. The root gave up its ink FILL when the pill became a card — inverting 240px reads as a hole in the page and would take the eye before the lime card that should have it — and carries its weight with a doubled ink border instead.
name: nodeShellClasses

description: Normalises a freshly extracted brief: CRLF and bare CR become newlines, trailing spaces and tabs are stripped from every line, runs of three or more newlines collapse to one paragraph break, and the document's own outer whitespace is trimmed. Everything downstream assumes this has run, so a .docx and a paste split into the same sections.
name: normalizeBriefText

description: The phase a stored string means, following the legacy aliases. Distinct from isPhase, which answers whether a value is literally one of the five current phases: the tool schema validates against the current vocabulary, while every path that READS a stored phase has to cope with what earlier versions wrote — chiefly 'deconstruct', which resolves to 'map'. Returns null for an unrecognised string so the caller picks its own fallback rather than being handed a wrong phase.
name: normalizePhase

description: Tells a subscribed agent the log moved. Reads the hook at call time rather than capturing it at module load, so a browser that gains the capability mid-session is picked up without a reload. Purely an optimisation that removes polling latency; a notification is not a turn and nothing depends on it.
name: notifyExchangeUpdated

untestabilityReason.justification: branches entirely on navigator.modelContext.notifyResourceUpdated, an unshipped W3C proposal no browser implements; the only reachable path today is the no-op

description: Reads a brief off an untrusted request body. A brief with no text in it is not a brief, and every way of expressing that - missing, empty, whitespace, wrongly typed, not an object - reduces to undefined so the caller has one case rather than five. The text is kept verbatim; a missing source name or media type falls back to the pasted defaults.
name: parseBriefInput

description: Reads a nudge batch off a request body, returning the parsed batch or the message to send back — the caller picks the status code, this decides what is acceptable. Offsets must be FINITE, not merely numeric: NaN and Infinity are both typeof number and either would put a node nowhere. One bad entry rejects the whole batch, since a partial arrangement is harder to explain than a refused one. Vestigial along with its route: nothing produces a nudge now that the map is a scrolling column of cards.
name: parseNudges

description: Reads a question's suggested answers out of the JSON array the column stores — SQLite has no array type. A missing, malformed, or wrongly-shaped value yields no chips at all, because a question with no shortlist is the ordinary case rather than a degraded one; blank and non-string entries are dropped so no unlabelled chip is ever rendered.
name: parseOptions

description: Reads a node id out of an event payload, returning null for anything that is not a non-empty string. Keeps a malformed event from contributing a phantom id to a round.
name: payloadId

description: Reads a phase name out of a phase.set payload, returning null for anything that is not a non-empty string. Lets a round be named after the phase it opened without a malformed payload blanking the row's eyebrow.
name: payloadPhase

description: The questions a pending ask_user is waiting on. The server writes them onto the map and returns this pending shape; only the page can perform the middle step of asking a person. Returns empty for an errored call or a result carrying none, which is the signal to hand the server's response straight back - putting a prompt on screen off the back of a failure would be worse than showing nothing.
name: pendingQuestions

description: What the page may honestly claim while it waits for the next round. The shimmering placeholder row is a promise, and WebMCP is pull-only — the page cannot start an agent's turn or know one is coming — so the shimmer is bounded and resolves into one of three genuinely different sentences: an agent is working and has the answers, an agent is attached but not in a turn, or nothing can reach the page and the answers are simply on the log. Hidden while the newest round still has open questions, and at next-steps where the loop arrives. Modelled on askPresence, which does the same job for the ask composer.
name: pendingRow

description: A phase's name for use in a sentence. The phase nav numbers its labels; the rail strips the number, so a row reads 'moved to Explore' rather than 'moved to 05 Explore'.
name: phaseName

description: Turns the model's tool calls into a validated plan of map changes without touching the database. Drops nodes whose kind the map cannot draw and nodes with blank labels, normalises an unknown status to answered, preserves insert order so a parent precedes the child that names it, and ignores an out-of-range phase. A slice's tests field is carried through as testsRef and deliberately NOT validated here: like parentRef it may name a node created earlier in the same call, so resolving it belongs to applyToolCalls, which can see the ids the database just handed back.
name: planMapMutations

description: Records something the person did onto the map's log. The tools run in the browser but the log lives in SQLite, so an answer only becomes durable - and only becomes visible to an agent on another front door - once it has come back through this route.
name: postUserEvent

untestabilityReason.justification: A single POST with no branching. The event kinds it may carry are enforced server-side by isUserEventKind, covered by app/lib/exchange.test.ts, and the answered path it serves is covered by answeredResponse in app/lib/toolInvocation.test.ts.

description: Publishes a headless driver on window over the same bound catalog. Not a debug convenience: WebMCP is top-level-secure-context only and codeyam renders the app inside a capture iframe, so navigator.modelContext is genuinely absent in every preview and captured scenario, and this driver is what makes the tools exercisable there at all. It calls the exact catalog entries a real agent would.
name: publishAgentDriver

description: The node ids a question.asked event announced. Tolerates a malformed or absent payload, because the log carries untrusted JSON that may predate the current shape.
name: questionIds

description: Turns the raw exchange log into the lines the activity rail shows, oldest first. Composes the three rules below: drop the bookkeeping, collapse runs, word what is left.
name: railEntries

description: Everything that happened after a cursor. An omitted cursor means the whole log, which is what a fresh agent wants; a cursor means just the delta, which is what a returning one wants. Both return the map's current revision, so a caller always leaves holding a cursor it can resume from even when the delta is empty.
name: readSince

description: The only place a map revision is minted. Appends events to the map's log and bumps ThinkingMap.revision once per event inside a single transaction, so a revision can never exist without its event or vice versa - either would hand a reader a cursor it cannot resume from. Every row of a batch carries the requestId, so a retry returns the whole original batch and its LAST revision; keying only the first row loses the batch's extent and hands a retrying agent a stale cursor, which makes it re-read its own writes as new. Fires the in-process emitter that waiting callers race against.
name: recordEvents

description: Renders the log one line per event: revision, kind, origin, and the gist. Because the exchange is pull-only, this text is the whole of what an agent learns about what happened while it was not looking. The revision leads each line because it is what the agent passes back as its cursor, and the gist is pulled from whichever payload field that kind uses.
name: renderEvents

description: Closes the open questions an answer resolved, logging one node.updated per node that actually moved. Answering the same question twice logs the second answer without inventing a second change, and a node the agent has since deleted is skipped rather than failing the write.
name: resolveAnswered

description: The readable part of an MCP tool response — the first text block, which is what an agent would actually read. Falls back to raw JSON rather than rendering nothing, because a silently empty panel is worse than an ugly one.
name: resultText

description: The line above a row, naming what the round was. A round that is entirely questions says so, because the question count is what the person is being asked to deal with; a mixed round counts nodes instead, since naming the majority kind would misdescribe it. The opening round is named for the idea rather than numbered. A research round is the exception that says what it IS rather than how many of anything it holds - what already exists is the thing somebody scanning the column is looking for, and a node count is not.
name: roundEyebrow

description: How far through a round the person is — the definition the whole feature gates on: the footer's count, whether the next row is reached for, and whether the phase's action appears. Counts only ANSWERABLE cards: a goal or assumption the agent has not filled in carries status 'open' and shows in the map caption, but has no answer box, so counting it would leave the loop permanently one short and the next row never reached for.
name: roundProgress

description: How far a collapsible run of adds or updates extends from an index. An agent turn that writes six nodes is one thing that happened, not six. Returns 1 for anything not collapsible, so the caller can always advance by the result.
name: runLength

description: Validates and runs one catalog tool. Agent input is untrusted, so it is checked against the tool's own schema before reaching an implementation and a validation failure comes back as readable text. isError is reserved for genuine faults: a conflict or a timeout is a normal result the agent is expected to reason about, and flagging those as errors would invite the blind retry the conflict path exists to prevent. Every front door - page, HTTP, stdio - ends here, which is what stops the three drifting apart.
name: runTool

description: Cuts the log's node-adds into runs, starting a new one whenever the writing side changes or the revisions stop being contiguous. A non-add event between two adds breaks contiguity, which is exactly right: ask_user writes its questions and then a question.asked, so a later add_nodes is genuinely a later turn.
name: runsFromLog

description: Builds one BriefSection from an index, a heading and a body - trimming the body and deriving its character count so the outline can be trusted without any passage being read.
name: section

description: Renders a brief section id as a person reads it - s7 becomes the section mark for 7. The id is the address the splitter derives, a node stores in sourceRef, and read_brief takes; the mark is only ever its display. Extracted from four inline copies across three components, which was three chances for the brief panel and a node pill to call the same section two different things.
name: sectionLabel

description: Turns a model's suggested answers into the JSON array the column stores, dropping the field entirely unless at least one usable string survives — so an agent sending an empty list or a list of blanks produces a plain question rather than a node carrying an array nothing can render. Non-strings are filtered rather than coerced, because a numeric option is a mistake and stringifying it would hide one.
name: serialiseOptions

description: The sentence the bounded shimmer resolves into, for each of the three things that can be true about who can hear the log: an agent mid-turn has what was added, an agent is attached but not in a turn, or nothing can reach the page at all. The three are deliberately distinct claims — collapsing them would make the page sound more attended-to than it is. Says what you have added rather than your answers, because the same row appears on a day-one map that has only a seed idea. Exported so the isolated-component fixtures cite the real sentence instead of a hand-copy that can drift.
name: settledNote

description: Splits an assistant reply into renderable lines and marks the ones that are questions, so the conversation panel can give them typographic weight. Only a line ending in a question mark counts; a mid-sentence question mark is usually the partner quoting the person back.
name: splitAssistantLines

description: Cuts a brief into stable, addressable sections - s1..sN with a heading, body and character count each. Splits on markdown headings where the document has them and groups paragraphs to a target size where it does not. Pure, so the same immutable text always yields the same ids without a table to keep in sync; an empty document returns no sections rather than one empty one.
name: splitIntoSections

description: Splits a document on its markdown headings, one section per heading. Prose before the first heading becomes its own section rather than being dropped - it is usually the summary - and a heading with nothing under it is kept, because a section the client left empty is part of the document's shape.
name: splitOnHeadings

description: Groups paragraphs up to a target size when a document has no headings, so plain prose still comes back as a readable handful of passages. A single paragraph over the maximum is left whole: an oversized passage beats one severed mid-argument.
name: splitOnParagraphs

description: Picks the one readable field worth showing for an event, in preference order - label, then text, then phase, then answer. Each event kind carries its human-readable part under a different name, and an agent reading a wall of bare kinds learns nothing about what changed.
name: summarize

description: Renders the current map as an indented outline carrying each node's real id, kind and status. This is the context the model reads before every turn, and the ids are what let it target an existing node with update_node.
name: summarizeMap

description: Holds text selection off for the duration of a drag and returns the restore function. Scoped to the gesture rather than the map, because selecting a node's label is worth keeping — it is how you copy one out.
name: suppressTextSelection

description: Wraps a string in the content envelope every MCP tool response takes. A one-line shape adapter with no branches; the strings it wraps are built by mcpFormat.
name: textResult

untestabilityReason.justification: A single return statement building the SDK's response literal - no branches, no transformation. The text it wraps comes from formatMapList and formatMapDetail, both covered by app/lib/mcpFormat.test.ts, and the envelope shape itself was verified against a live MCP client over both transports.

description: How deep a thread bends, given the vertical gap between two rows: two thirds of the gap, clamped at both ends.
