The floor exists because a straight line between two rows reads as a table rule rather than a thread; the ceiling exists because past it the control points overshoot their own endpoints and the curve loops back on itself. Between the clamps the bend tracks the gap, so a taller gap gets a lazier curve rather than the same one stretched.
name: threadPull

description: Clamps an agent's requested wait into milliseconds: a default when none is given, a ceiling so a confused agent cannot pin a connection open indefinitely, and a one-second floor so a wait never degrades into a busy loop.
name: timeoutMsFrom

description: The catalog as a browser agent or the headless driver lists it. A tool missing here is a tool the agent never learns it can call, so it is derived from the catalog rather than restated.
name: toolSummaries

description: The sentence a person sends the agent when they notice a brief section nobody has dealt with. It rides the existing user.note channel, so the wording IS the whole message - nothing else carries the intent. It names the section twice over, by mark and by heading, so the agent can go straight to it rather than re-reading the outline, and it asks a question rather than only reporting an absence, because the point is to get the section dealt with on the next turn.
name: untouchedNoteText

description: Moving the map to its next phase, from the page — the first page-side caller of set_phase, which until now only ever moved because an agent moved it. The ORDER is the point: the note saying what was decided goes on the log BEFORE the phase moves, so an agent reading the log finds a sentence rather than a phase that silently changed under it. A failed phase write therefore leaves the decision recorded, and says so rather than claiming the note was lost.
name: useAdvancePhase

description: The ask_user promise lifecycle: park an agent's turn on a set of questions, and release it when they are answered or the clock runs out. Separate from the log because it is a different clock — the log is durable and outlives everyone, this is one turn held in memory. A second ask releases the first as unanswered rather than stranding its promise.
name: useAskUser

description: How long something has been true, reported once it has been true long enough — the only input the pending row needs that a pure function cannot compute. Reports a STEP rather than a ticking clock, 0 until the limit then the limit, because a value changing every frame would re-render the whole map column to move a decision that flips exactly once. Restarts on its reset key, so a new round means the page is reaching for something new rather than still waiting on the old.
name: useBoundedWait

description: The page's own copy of the exchange log, kept current. Polls the log forward from the cursor it holds — the same way an agent reads it, because WebMCP is pull-only and there is no push channel — and re-renders the server component when the log moves past what was rendered, so the server-rendered map does not sit out of step with its own log.
name: useExchangeLog

description: Keeping the bottom of a growing column in view, for a reader who is already at the bottom and nobody else. Two subtleties: it must not fire on first paint, because a page that jumps to its own bottom before the person has read the top is not reacting to anything; and 'have I run before' is the wrong way to express that, since StrictMode invokes effects twice on mount and would consume such a flag — so the refs are seeded with mount-time values during render and the effect compares against a transition instead.
name: useFollowColumn

description: What every question on the map has been answered, and how to answer one. Merges the log's answers with an optimistic layer for answers written in this tab: the answer takes the card's body the moment it is sent, because one still sitting in the input after you pressed send reads as the answer having been lost, and it is rolled back only if the write actually failed. The pending entry is never cleared on success — the log catches up on its own, and clearing early would flicker the question back to unanswered.
name: useMapAnswers

description: The bridge if there is one, null if there is not. For a component that renders in both the app and an isolated scenario, where the throwing accessor would make the second case a crash rather than a state. Anything that genuinely needs the exchange still uses useWebMcpBridge and says so by throwing.
name: useOptionalWebMcpBridge

untestabilityReason.justification: a single useContext read with no branching logic; the state it returns is exercised through the components that consume it

description: Reads the bridge state - connection status, the questions an agent is waiting on, the current revision, and the two writers - from context. Throws outside a provider rather than returning a null the caller would have to guard at every use site.
name: useWebMcpBridge

untestabilityReason.justification: A useContext read with a single null check and no other branching. The state it exposes is produced by the WebMcpBridge component, which is covered by the mid-exchange scenario.

description: Checks an agent's call against the tool it named and returns either the parsed input or the response to send back. Runs on the page as well as the server - not redundantly, but because it turns a malformed call into an immediate readable answer rather than a round trip, and agent input is untrusted on both sides of the wire. The message names the offending field so the agent can correct itself instead of guessing.
name: validateToolInput

description: The events worth showing a person, with the bookkeeping dropped. Hides the open-question nodes that ask_user created when a question.asked announced them, and the node.updated that closes a question the person just answered — both are cases where one act produced two events. An agent's own update to the same node still shows.
name: visibleEvents

description: Blocks until somebody starts a thinking map, or until the caller's timeout expires. The server-door half of the answer to a page not being able to wake an agent: nothing here pushes, but an agent with nothing to do can park, so a submitted idea is picked up rather than sitting on an empty page. A near-copy of waitForUserActivity - check first, then race the in-process emitter against a poll, on a bounded deadline - so the two read as one pattern. Cursored by createdAt rather than revision, because revision is per-map and a map that does not exist yet has none a waiter could have read. The comparison is exclusive, which is what stops a re-park from re-delivering the map just handed over. A timeout is a normal result carrying the cursor, never an error.
name: waitForNewMap

description: Blocks until the person contributes, or until the caller's timeout expires. Re-reads the log first because an event may already be waiting and a waiter that subscribed before checking would sleep through it; then races an in-process emitter against a ~500ms poll. The poll is what lets a write from the separate stdio process wake a waiter living in the web process - an emitter alone would be silently correct in dev and silently wrong across front doors. Always resolves: a timeout is a normal result carrying the cursor, never a hang.
name: waitForUserActivity

description: Why the page is not bound, in words the UI can show honestly. Each reason names a different fix, so they deliberately do not collapse into one generic unavailable the person cannot act on. The security gates are reported before the missing-agent gate so an insecure page is told to fix that first.
name: webMcpUnavailableReason

description: Names the side that acted — 'Agent' or 'You'. The map is co-authored, so every rail line has to attribute itself; an unrecognised origin falls through as itself rather than becoming an anonymous row.
name: who
